messages:
alice: Customer ACME on Dedicated pool dc-redwood-37 reporting a ~40% TPS drop since ~13:00 UTC. 429s increasing, p50->p95 latency spike to ~600ms. Route /v1/generate, model=llama-2-13b-q4. Can someone take a look?

ben: Looking. Do we have autoscaler events or any noisy-tenant spikes? Also need continuous-batcher metrics (pending_tokens, max_batch_tokens, batch_window_ms).

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled down pool dc-redwood-37 from 10 -> 6 at 13:08:12Z (scale_reason=cpu_idle). No recent crashloop detected.

caro: I pulled route logs, a lot of requests are hitting short sequences but returning larger outputs. Might be KV cache miss pattern + big max_batch_tokens causing oversized micro-batches.

david: Share the metrics dump link pls (5m window). I'll check scheduler utilization.

alice: metrics: http://int-metrics.internal/dedicated/dc-redwood-37?window=5m (internal). Key ones I watched: continuous_batcher.pending_tokens jumped, batch_success_rate down, scheduler_queue_depth up. Also saw token_scheduler.latency tail increase.

ben: If pending_tokens >> max_batch_tokens we can get very uneven batching where small requests wait for large ones. What is max_batch_tokens set to for this route?

caro: config snippet for that pool/route: ```
route: /v1/generate
model: llama-2-13b-q4
max_batch_tokens: 8192
batch_window_ms: 25
per_tenant_queue_limit: 500
```

david: 8192 is high given request shape (mostly 64-512 input tokens). With a few long outputs we're filling batch tokens and starving many small requests. Suggest lowering max_batch_tokens or enabling token-aware fairqueue.

alice: Customer also reported a couple of 429s that look like our rate limiter, maybe because queue depth triggered fast-path rejects. Billing/auth looks ok, not quota.

oncall: @ben @david I can do a quick config patch for the pool. Proposed temporary mitigations:
- set max_batch_tokens=4096
- set batch_window_ms=12
- enable token_aware_fairqueue=true
- apply per-tenant qlimit=250

ben: Agreed. Quick note: this is a low-risk runtime change (no model reload). I'll patch the rollout to 50% of nodes first.

ben: kubectl command to patch route config (internal):
```
kubectl -n runtime patch configroute dc-redwood-37 --type=json -p='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/routes/0/max_batch_tokens","value":4096}, {"op":"replace","path":"/routes/0/batch_window_ms","value":12} ]'
```

caro: Also patch scheduler: enable per-tenant token fairqueue flag:
```
PUT /internal/pools/dc-redwood-37/config
{ "token_aware_fairqueue": true, "per_tenant_queue_limit": 250 }
```

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-387 created for ACME: throughput drop on dedicated, assigned to @eng-runtime.

ben: Patching 50% -> applied to nodes {n1,n2,n3,n4}. Observing metrics.

infra-bot: config-apply: change propagated to 4/8 nodes at 13:22:45Z.

david: Early telemetry: pending_tokens down ~60%, scheduler_queue_depth normalizing, p95 latency dropping from 600ms -> ~220ms. No 429s observed in the last 90s.

alice: Can we run a short repro load to validate behavior and ensure no regression in throughput or cost? Provide a simple repro script.

david: Quick reproducible load (example):
```
# spawn 200 parallel requests with small inputs
seq 1 200 | xargs -P50 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"llama-2-13b-q4","input":"summarize: short text","max_tokens":128}' &
```

caro: Ran that against the patched nodes, result: throughput returned to baseline and tail latency improved. We still see a few larger requests causing transient queueing but overall fairer distribution.

ben: Follow-ups: 1) add regression alert for large delta between pending_tokens and max_batch_tokens, 2) consider auto-tune for max_batch_tokens per-route based on recent token length histogram, 3) add a canary that simulates mixed short/long request shapes before scale-down decisions.

oncall: Agreed. I'll open infra tickets for auto-tune and canary. For ACME I'll keep Dedicated pool pinned while they validate for next 24h.

alice: ACME confirms degraded->healthy in their test runs. Thanks team. Closing initial escalation but keeping ticket open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-387 updated: status=monitoring, assignees=[ben, david], priority=high.

ben: Note for postmortem: autoscaler scaled down at 13:08 because CPU looked idle while queueing metrics were rising. Need a decider that considers scheduler_queue_depth/pending_tokens before scale-down.

david: Filed PR to add queue-aware autoscale heuristic, assigning reviewers. PR#runt-512.

alice: Great, thanks everyone. We'll circle back after the 24h validation window.
